## 1500 W Wilson Ave — Zoning & Development Analysis
**PIN: 14171060250000** | Uptown (Community Area 3) | Ward 47

---

### 1. Zoning District

This parcel is zoned **B1-2** (Neighborhood Shopping District, Dash-2 bulk/density). This is confirmed by the City's official GIS parcel records. Verify at the [Chicago Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning).

---

### 2. Residential Uses: Apartments Above Retail & Ground-Floor Units

**Above ground floor:** B1 districts permit residential dwelling units **on or above the ground floor** — however, the retrieved code text for B1 specifically was not included in the retrieved sections. The closely adjacent B2 district explicitly permits residential "on or above the ground floor" [1]. The B3 district permits residential **above** the ground floor [1]. For B1, the standard interpretation in Chicago's zoning framework is that residential is permitted **above** but not on the ground floor in neighborhood shopping districts — but you should confirm the exact B1 use table with the Department of Planning & Development (DPD) or via Chicago Municipal Code [2] § 17-3-0200 (use standards for B districts), which was not retrieved here.

**Ground-floor apartments:** In B districts generally, ground-floor residential is not the intended use. Ground-floor conversion of commercial space to residential is possible under a specific exception: the Zoning Administrator may approve conversion of an occupied or vacant commercial establishment below the second floor into residential dwelling units pursuant to [3]. This is not a by-right entitlement — it requires administrative approval.

*Confidence: Moderate. The B1 use table (§ 17-3-0200) was not retrieved; the above reflects general B-district structure.*

---

### 3. Key Bulk & Density Standards (B1-2)

The dash-2 designation sets the applicable bulk tier [1]. The specific B1-2 standards table (§ 17-3-0403 et seq.) was not fully retrieved, but the framework is:

- **FAR:** B districts have maximum FAR set by the standards table in [3]. For B1-2, FAR is typically **2.2** — but this figure was **not confirmed in the retrieved text**; verify via DPD or § 17-3-0403-A [3].
- **Maximum height:** Set by the dash-2 designation; typically **38 feet** in B1-2 — again, not confirmed in retrieved text. Verify § 17-3-0404.
- **Minimum lot area per dwelling unit:** Set in § 17-3-0405; not retrieved — verify with DPD.
- **Front setback:** No minimum front setback is generally required in B districts (build-to requirement on pedestrian streets, but this parcel is **not** on a designated pedestrian street per the overlay data).
- **Side & rear setbacks:** B district standards apply per § 17-3-0406; residential floors above commercial may trigger rear setback requirements. The residential open space and setback rules in [2] apply to any dwelling units included.
- **Open space:** Required open space for residential units may not be satisfied by parking areas or driveways [2].

*Confidence: Low-to-moderate on specific numbers — the B1-2 standards table was not in the retrieved code chunks. Use DPD's Zoning Help Line or the Chicago Zoning Ordinance § 17-3-0400 directly.*

---

### 4. Overlays & Special Designations

- **Transit-Oriented Development (CTA):** Yes — this parcel is in a CTA TOD overlay. Nearest CTA rail is Montrose (Brown Line), 0.45 miles away; nearest Metra is Ravenswood (UP North), 0.39 miles away.
- **Transit-Oriented Development (Metra):** Also applies — dual TOD coverage.
- **ADU Eligible Area:** Yes — accessory dwelling units are permitted here under Chicago's ADU ordinance (pilot area).
- **Affordable Requirements Ordinance (ARO) Zone:** Yes — any residential project triggering an ARO entitlement (typically 10+ units with city financial assistance or a zoning change) must comply with affordability requirements. The Uptown community area has 20 ARO-tracked projects with 976 total affordable units.
- **Special Service Area:** This parcel is in **SSA — Greater Ravenswood**, which levies a supplemental tax for area services and improvements (note: SSA 31 also appears in the tax breakdown below).
- **Planned Development:** No.
- **Landmark/Historic District:** No — not in a landmark or historic district, not on the National Register.
- **Lakefront Protection:** No.
- **Flood Zone:** FEMA Zone **X** (Area of Minimal Flood Hazard) — not a Special Flood Hazard Area; flood insurance is not required.
- **Brownfields:** None identified nearby.

---

### 5. Parking Requirement & Transit Reduction

Because this parcel is in a CTA TOD overlay, the minimum off-street parking requirement **can be reduced by up to 100%** under [3] §17-10-0102-B. In plain terms: **you may be able to build with zero required parking** at this location. This relief is available by right for a B1-2 parcel in a TOD area — no special entitlement is required for the parking reduction itself.

---

### 6. Maximum Height, FAR, and What Transit Changes

**FAR and height:** As noted in Part 3, the by-right maximum FAR and height for B1-2 are set in § 17-3-0403-A and § 17-3-0404 — **these figures were not confirmed in the retrieved code text**. Verify directly.

**Does transit proximity allow more density or FAR?** The FAR increase for transit-served locations under [3] applies **only in B-3 and C-3 districts** (dash-3 designations) within 2,640 feet of a CTA/Metra rail station or 1,320 feet of a qualifying CTA bus corridor — and even then, it requires a Type 1 Zoning Map Amendment, Planned Development approval, or an ARO entitlement trigger [3]. This parcel is zoned B1-**2**, not a dash-3 district, so **no FAR or density bonus is available by right**, and no height bonus applies here [3]. There is no density, FAR, or height bonus at B1-2 — those benefits apply only in dash-3 districts.

**What transit does change here:** Parking only (up to 100% reduction, as above). The parcel's Walk Score of 95/100 (Walker's Paradise), Transit Score of 81/100 (Excellent Transit), and Bike Score of 91/100 (Biker's Paradise) reinforce the practical case for reduced-parking development, but these do not affect the legal zoning standards.

---

### Financial Context

The parcel is in the **Clark/Montrose TIF district** (established 1999, expires **2035**), with a current fund balance of ~$14.0M and cumulative revenue of ~$71.1M. TIF increment financing may be available for qualifying projects — active projects include the Black Ensemble Studio Theater and the SBIF small business grant program. The estimated annual property tax is **$15,960** (2024 rates), primarily to the Board of Education ($8,539), City of Chicago ($3,798), and Cook County ($918). The property has a standard tax class (517) with no incentive reduction.
